tools.name: execute
tools.description:
Run JavaScript in a sandbox against the documentation at https://redocly.com. The script calls the sandbox functions on the global `site` object.
The only extra global is `site` - there is no `fetch`, `console`, `setTimeout`, `require`, or Node.js API; all I/O goes through `site`.

Workflow - minimi

tools.name: discover
tools.description:
Get the exact TypeScript signatures of the sandbox functions that `execute` scripts can call.
Analyze the user request first, then pass `names` with only the functions the request needs (every name is listed in this input schema / description); omit `names` only when you cannot tell which functions

tools.name: submit-feedback
tools.description: Report a documentation page that is wrong or incomplete. Use it when the user reports a problem with a page on this site, or agrees to report a problem that you found. Do not use it for product bugs or support questions.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "execute" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "execute" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "discover" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
